title: UCSD Decorator chrome selector contract
description: Declarative require/forbid rules evaluated against the protected chrome regions of a rendered Decorator page. This is the tier that encodes what the chrome is FOR, so it must not be satisfiable by regenerating a golden fingerprint.

derivedFrom.description: Provenance. Present on generated files, absent on hand-maintained overlays.

id.description: Stable identifier, reported as chrome/structure/<id>. Overlays override derived rules by matching id.

region.description: Which protected chrome region this rule applies to.

within.description: Optional CSS selector narrowing the scope inside the region.

source.description: Path to the file this rule was derived from, printed in failure output so an agent knows where to restore markup from.

remedy.description: One or two sentences telling the reader what to do. Printed on failure.

requirement.description: A count assertion (selector + count), an attribute assertion (attribute + equals/equalsUrl/absent, optionally targeted by selector), or a text assertion (selector + hasText).

count.description: Exact number of matches required. Defaults to 1.

equalsUrl.description: Attribute value compared after stripping the deployment base path, so one rule holds for every deployment mode. Use this for any href/src/action.

absent.description: The attribute must not be present.

hasText.description: Every element matching selector must contain non-whitespace text. Pairs with a region's ignoreTextOf: tier 2 lets the wording change, and this keeps it from being emptied.

reason.description: Why this is prohibited. Printed on failure, so write it for someone who thinks their substitution was reasonable.
